Synopsis:
Petrobras is preparing a ~1 BRL/liter diesel price hike at its refineries, contingent on the Brazilian government rolling out a new consumer subsidy of equivalent size (stacked on top of an existing ~1.12 BRL/liter subsidy). The driver is a widening gap between domestic diesel prices and international benchmarks, inflated by Middle East tensions and Russian diesel export restrictions. As Brazil imports ~25% of its diesel needs, the margin squeeze is material to Petrobras profitability. The hike aims to near-fully close the import parity gap.
